rationale: Both documents treat the source as something the method builds on and is a variant of (credits level): the write-up calls it the "white-bear" steering direction and frames its own think-vs-neutral contrast as a deliberate departure from the prior think-vs-don't-think contrast, while the message describes the same relationship almost identically, including matching numbers (0.677 vs 0.608) and the same control/novelty-check results. The only material difference is that the message explicitly names the source as "Raman, in your papers/", giving a concrete attribution the write-up omits (the write-up only uses the unattributed term "white-bear" in quotes); otherwise the overlap and novelty claims (shared axis, different contrast, no off-axis alternative found) are presented equivalently in both.
